title: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom in Chinese: Hong Xiuquan's Yuandao tracts, the imperially sanctioned books (旨准頒行詔書) including the Taiping Old and New Testaments (1853), Yang Xiuqing's descents as the Heavenly Father, the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle and Hong Rengan's New Treatise (1859)
edition: 原道救世歌、原道醒世訓、原道覺世訓 — Hong Xiuquan, the three Yuandao tracts (c. 1845–48), transcluded on Wikisource from the scan of 太平天國史料 第1集 (1950); 天父上帝言題皇詔 — the Heavenly Father's edict; 天父下凡詔書 (第一部、第二部) — the Heavenly Father's descent: Yang Xiuqing speaking as God (1851–53); 天命詔旨書 — Book of Heavenly Decrees and Proclamations (太平天囯壬子二年新刻, 1852); 欽定舊遺詔聖書 — the Old Testament as revised by Hong Xiuquan (太平天囯癸好三年新刻, 1853), six juan; 欽定前遺詔聖書 — the New Testament as revised by Hong Xiuquan (太平天囯癸好三年新刻, 1853); the Gospel of John (juan 4) wanting on Wikisource; 天條書 — the Book of Heavenly Commandments (太平天囯癸好三年鐫刻, 1853); 頒行詔書 — the proclamations of Yang Xiuqing and Xiao Chaogui; 三字經 (太平天國) — the Taiping Three Character Classic; 幼學詩 — Ode for Youth (太平天囯壬子二年新刻, 1852); 太平條規 — the Taiping regulations; 太平禮制 — the Taiping ceremonial (太平天囯戊午八年新刻, 1858); 天朝田畝制度 — the Land System of the Heavenly Dynasty (1853); 天情道理書 — the Book of the Principles of the Heavenly Nature (太平天囯甲寅四年新刻, 1854); 天理要論 — Essentials of Heavenly Principle (太平天囯甲寅四年新刻, 1854); 太平救世歌 — Yang Xiuqing, the Taiping Song of World Salvation; 太平天日 — the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle: Hong Xiuquan's vision of 1837, proclaimed in 戊申 (1848) and printed in 壬戌十二年 (1862); 資政新篇 — Hong Rengan, A New Treatise on Aids to Administration (1859)

normalization: Each page fetched from Chinese Wikisource at a recorded revision (oldid), twice: its wikitext (original/wikisource/wikitext/) and its rendered HTML (original/wikisource/html/, action=render at that oldid). The text layer (text/<slug>.txt) is derived from the rendered HTML by rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-24/taiping_text.py: the header table, the licence banner and print-suppressed elements dropped, line breaks kept, pages of a work joined in order under '=== <title> (oldid N) ==='. Characters as Wikisource gives them, with the Taiping forms (囯, 眞) the transcribers keep. Wikisource's own text-quality notes are in the wikitext.
scope: The texts of the Taiping movement as Wikisource holds them: Hong Xiuquan's three Yuandao tracts, written in the years after his vision and before the rising (c. 1845–48); the books issued under the Heavenly King's seal (旨准頒行詔書), of which the movement's own list names twenty-nine, seated here as Wikisource has them: the Heavenly Father's edict, the two parts of the Heavenly Father's descent, the Book of Heavenly Decrees (1852), the Old and New Testaments as Hong revised and annotated them (1853), the Heavenly Commandments (1853), the proclamations, the Three Character Classic, the Ode for Youth (1852), the regulations, the ceremonial (1858), the Land System (1853), the Principles of the Heavenly Nature and the Essentials of Heavenly Principle (1854); Yang Xiuqing's Taiping Song of World Salvation; the Taiping Heavenly Chronicle (proclaimed 1848, printed 1862); and Hong Rengan's New Treatise (1859). Not seated: the books of the list Wikisource does not hold, among them the Taiping Imperial Declaration (太平詔書), the army organization (太平軍目) and the calendar (頒行曆書), and the Gospel of John of the Taiping New Testament: QUEUED, as are scans of the original Nanjing imprints (British Library and others) and the Taiping documents in Western collections. Translations (Medhurst, 1853; Michael, 1966–71) are not seated.

Tianchao tianmu zhidu, the nine grades of land — '凡田分九等'
Youxue shi, the first ode — '眞神皇上帝 萬囯盡尊崇'

why_seated: The fourth tradition of 1844: in that year Hong Xiuquan and Feng Yunshan went out preaching into Guangxi, where the God Worshippers' Society took shape and from which the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom rose in 1851. Its scripture is a Bible rewritten and annotated by its king, beside the words of a God who spoke through Yang Xiuqing until Yang was killed in the Tianjing incident of 1856.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 27 October 2026: "need to seat the book of mormon but im not doing it without several diverging simultaneous traditions in the batch" — offered the traditions that divided in 1844 (the Latter Day Saint succession, the Bab's declaration, the Millerite disappointment, the Taiping beginnings), or the Book of Mormon's own editions — "1. definitely. lets go."
